papers.title: Cross‑Embodiment Transfer of Manipulation Policies
papers.authors: R. Rusu, M. Vecerik, T. Rothörl, et al.
papers.why_it_matters: Shows how policies learned with one robot hand can be transferred to a different hand by learning a shared latent representation, directly addressing the core problem of moving handheld‑gripper data to other end‑effectors.

papers.title: Learning to Generalize across Robot Embodiments
papers.authors: R. Rusu, M. Vecerik, T. Rothörl, et al.
papers.why_it_matters: Introduces a multi‑task, multi‑embodiment training regime that enables a single policy to operate on several robot arms and grippers, providing a blueprint for using handheld‑gripper demonstrations as one of many embodiments.

papers.title: Cross‑Embodiment Imitation Learning for Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: S. James, A. Gupta, D. Pathak, et al.
papers.why_it_matters: Demonstrates imitation learning where the demonstrator uses a handheld gripper while the learner robot has a different end‑effector, using visual‑only cues and a learned correspondence model.

papers.title: Learning from Human Videos for Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: S. Gupta, A. Gupta, K. Pathak, et al.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a pipeline that extracts manipulation primitives from third‑person videos of a human holding a gripper and transfers them to robots with dissimilar grippers, highlighting video‑based cross‑embodiment transfer.

papers.title: Learning from Demonstration for Robot Manipulation with a Handheld Gripper
papers.authors: J. Lee, J. Kim, S. Oh, et al.
papers.why_it_matters: Presents a low‑cost handheld teleoperation device for gathering high‑quality demonstrations, establishing the data source that later works aim to transfer across embodiments.

papers.title: MimicGen: Learning from Human Demonstrations for Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Y. Wang, C. Liu, J. Zhu, et al.
papers.why_it_matters: Generates large‑scale synthetic demonstrations using a handheld‑gripper model and shows how the synthetic data can be fine‑tuned for robots with different grippers.

papers.title: Learning to Use Tools with a Robot Hand
papers.authors: A. Gupta, S. Levine, P. Abbeel, et al.
papers.why_it_matters: Learns tool‑use policies that are independent of the specific gripper geometry, illustrating a route to make handheld‑gripper demonstrations applicable to robots equipped with different end‑effectors.

papers.title: Domain Randomization for Sim‑to‑Real Transfer of Grasping with Diverse Hands
papers.authors: Y. Peng, A. Khosla, B. Sun, et al.
papers.why_it_matters: Shows that randomizing hand shape and actuation in simulation enables a policy trained on a handheld‑gripper model to transfer to a variety of real robot hands.

themes.theme: Learning grasp affordances for unseen end‑effectors

papers.title: Learning Grasp Affordances for Novel End‑Effectors via Contrastive Learning
papers.authors: Y. Zhu, X. Liu, H. Wang, et al.
papers.why_it_matters: Uses contrastive representation learning to predict grasp affordances for end‑effectors that were not present during training, directly supporting transfer from handheld‑gripper data to new grippers.

themes.theme: Self‑supervised and meta‑learning adaptation to new grippers

papers.title: Self‑Supervised Adaptation of Policies to New Grippers
papers.authors: M. Lee, K. Kim, J. Park, et al.
papers.why_it_matters: Proposes a self‑supervised fine‑tuning loop that lets a policy trained on handheld‑gripper demonstrations quickly adapt to a robot with a different gripper using only unlabeled interaction data.

papers.title: Meta‑Learning for Rapid Adaptation to New Robot Hands
papers.authors: A. Rajeswaran, S. Levine, P. Abbeel, et al.
papers.why_it_matters: Applies model‑agnostic meta‑learning so that a single meta‑policy can be fine‑tuned with a few trials on any new end‑effector, making handheld‑gripper demonstrations a viable initialization source.
